extracted.intended_audience: marketing and communications managers, comms professionals, and B2B tech companies evaluating or commissioning digital PR
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for measuring and reporting the effectiveness of digital and traditional PR campaigns, focused on metrics, analytics setup, SEO impact, and content optimisation for B2B tech brands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency of campaigns to truly measure PR success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should provide a more transparent view of campaigns and efforts so clients can trust reported outcomes; transparent reporting is a prerequisite for meaningful measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set clear goals and KPIs from the start
rubrics_metrics.description: Measuring PR is the way in which campaigns are tracked against metrics and KPIs to evaluate whether it was a success or a failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the beginning of any digital PR campaign establish clear goals/objectives and agree what the business is measuring as 'success'. An effective consultancy will work with you to set up measurable goals (see Google Analytics and CIPR-recommended goal types).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Advertising Value Equivalent (AVE)
rubrics_metrics.description: The dreaded Advertising Value Equivalent (AVE) - PR measurement has stopped short when it comes to reporting back on its efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AVE is presented as an outdated/unreliable metric; agencies and clients should avoid relying on AVE and instead use digital analytics and SEO-based measures that tie to business outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain Authority (DA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Domain Authority is a measure (ranked from 1-100) that describes which websites have the most trusted information and are more likely to be ranked by search engines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target placements on mainstream news and high-DA sites (BBC, Guardian, Forbes, government, university sites) because links from these domains have higher SEO value for your business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Followed vs nofollow links
rubrics_metrics.description: An earned follow link on a news website or blog essentially acts as an 'endorsement' ... Marking a link as 'no follow' removes this endorsement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tools like MOZ Bar to check link attributes. The more followed links from authoritative sites you earn, the greater the likely impact on SEO and search rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earned backlinks as an SEO metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Being able to earn backlinks to a client’s website from news websites is a key trait for modern digital PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative, informative content that journalists want to link to is essential; link-building via PR should be an explicit objective and reported as part of campaign success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral traffic and correlation to PR activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify increases in web traffic and referral traffic and how it correlates to PR activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review referral traffic from news websites/blogs where coverage appears to see whether visitors engage further, convert, or bounce. Correlate spikes in referral traffic with specific PR placements and timestamps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bounce rate in context
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a high 'bounce rate' (i.e. a visitor lands on your website, stays for a moment then leaves) don’t fear, as bounce rates cannot be viewed in isolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret bounce rates alongside other engagement and conversion metrics; consistently high bounce rates from referral traffic may indicate problems with website content or design that undermine PR effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website optimisation for PR conversions
rubrics_metrics.description: Your website needs to be user friendly and easy to navigate to engage your visitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimise H1 page headers, page titles and on-page content for target keywords; ensure landing pages are set up to convert referral traffic from PR into leads, downloads, or other agreed goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Google Analytics goal types (Destination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Destination goals – Getting visitors to a particular page on your site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use destination goals to track conversions tied to PR (e.g., thank-you pages after a download or form submission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Google Analytics goal types (Time on site)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time on site – This is one measure of an ‘engagement goal’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as an engagement indicator; longer time can suggest content relevance but should be interpreted with other metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Google Analytics goal types (Pages per session)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of pages visited per session – Another engagement goal and is a way of measuring whether your visitors are exploring your website for information or simply leaving after that initial click through.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher pages-per-session implies deeper engagement from PR-driven visitors; use to assess whether PR content attracts meaningful interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Google Analytics goal types (Event goal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Event goal - This metric can measure the general behaviour of your visitors e.g. are they watching any videos or downloading a report?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrument events (video plays, downloads, clicks) to capture non-pageview conversions driven by PR and measure content engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure whether PR is reaching the right audience
rubrics_metrics.description: If you’re seeing a consistent spike in web traffic throughout a PR campaign, but little to no conversions it could suggest the audience you're attracting isn’t the right audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether target publications are read by the audiences who could do business with you; retarget or refocus on different media verticals if referral traffic doesn't convert.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure pages contributing to ROI
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting up goals and effective reporting can also give you insight into how much each website page is contributing to the overall ROI of your PR campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute conversions and revenue (where possible) to specific referral pages to report success of individual campaigns and inform future content direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media metrics for PR (followers, engagement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key metrics to measure are pretty obvious in the sense of followers ... whether you are getting likes, comments and re-tweets for the content you publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track follower growth, engagement rates (likes/comments/shares), mentions, and the profile of followers to gauge awareness and interest driven by PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social mentions and sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the number of mentions your business gets; and the sentiment of those mentions – either positive or negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure sentiment shifts during/after campaigns and use social listening to see what conversations your brand appears in; sentiment recovery speed is a crisis-communications KPI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis communications metric: speed to sentiment recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: If your brand becomes subject to negative news attention on social media, a key metric to establishing whether your crisis communications strategy is working is how quickly those negative communications and interactions on social media give way to more positive responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track time-to-recovery and sentiment trendlines after interventions to evaluate crisis handling effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use social media monitoring to surface opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Using social media monitoring as part of your PR campaign - like those which journalists use themselves - means you are always aware of what the latest topic of conversation is in your industry and can quickly react with your own content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor emerging threads and conversations to pitch relevant content, identify influencers, and react quickly to be considered a thought leader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure how hard content is working (repurposing & reach)
rubrics_metrics.description: A key metric in PR measurement is how hard your content is working for you ... repurposing content over numerous platforms and measuring which has most success means you can create more effective campaigns further down the road.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track performance of the same content across formats/platforms (whitepaper → article → blog → social posts) to identify which versions drive the best engagement and conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer digital/SEO-based measures over print-only circulation estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: In the past measuring estimated circulation and audience figures to the dreaded AVE - PR measurement has stopped short. PR has shifted towards online and digital platforms, allowing agencies to use analytics platforms to track its efforts and success through metrics that directly affect the website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, prioritise web analytics, referral attribution, and SEO signals (links, DA) that connect PR activity to business outcomes rather than relying solely on print circulation figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency competency: journalist relationships and media targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Your PR consultancy should have strong relationships with journalists in their chosen industries, and therefore a route to gaining press coverage on those high domain authority news websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing an agency look for evidence of media relationships, clear advice on which media to target, and alignment between publication audiences and your target customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch thought leadership and provide linkable assets
rubrics_metrics.description: You need to create content which the press will want to print, and then ensure you have additional content which adds extra value which a journalist will want to link back to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop thought leadership pieces and supporting assets (whitepapers, research, data) as linkable resources to increase the likelihood of follow links and SEO benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tools and SEO reporting to show a direct measurable link
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting your business featured on a website with a high domain authority with a follow link in the article ... is also much more beneficial for your online visibility and forms a direct measurable link through SEO reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SEO tools and analytics to demonstrate how earned links and placements affect rankings, organic traffic, and conversions so stakeholders can see tangible ROI from PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious of in-house obscure metrics; prefer verifiable analytics
rubrics_metrics.description: To try and justify investment in the past, PR professionals have come up with many metrics over the years, from obscure measurements developed in house, to the always to be avoided 'advertising value equivalent'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer standardised, verifiable metrics (GA goals, referral traffic, link metrics, DA, conversions) over opaque in-house formulas that cannot be independently validated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value different types of earned print coverage appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: The different types of earned print media coverage - Leads, Downpages and News In Brief (NIB): Leads: a lead story ... Downpage: below the fold ... News In Brief: short and snappy pieces
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise qualitative differences between lead stories, downpage placements and NIBs; leads generally give more prominence and potential impact, while NIBs are useful but limited—question a consultancy that only delivers NIBs.
